Plot how a feature's SHAP value is assembled from components

Source: R/plot_shap_decomposition.R
plot_shap_decomposition.Rd

For one observation, shows the components involving each selected feature, starting at the intercept E[f]. Interaction terms are split evenly among their features, so each feature's bars sum to its SHAP value, shown in the bottom row. To see the whole prediction instead, use plot_waterfall() or plot_force().

Usage

plot_shap_decomposition(
  object,
  id,
  threshold = NULL,
  max_interaction = NULL,
  predictors = NULL,
  class = NULL,
  barheight = 0.5
)

glex_explain(...)

Arguments

object

Object of class glex containing prediction components and data to be explained.

id

(integer(1)) Row ID of the observation to be explained in object$x.

threshold

(numeric(1): NULL) Terms whose contribution is at or below this are aggregated under a "Remaining terms" label. The default NULL uses 2.5% of the largest absolute contribution in each panel; set 0 to show all terms.

max_interaction

(integer(1): NULL) Terms of a higher degree are aggregated under the "Remaining terms" label.

predictors

(character: NULL) Vector of column names in $x to restrict the plot to.

class

(character: NULL) For multiclass targets, the target classes to show.

barheight

(numeric(1): 0.5) Relative height of the bars.

...

Arguments passed to plot_shap_decomposition().

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The plot can get busy; use predictors, max_interaction, or threshold to restrict it.

See also

Other Visualization functions: plot.glex(), plot.glex_vi(), plot_force(), plot_pdp(), plot_waterfall()

Examples

set.seed(1)
library(randomPlantedForest)
rp <- rpf(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars[1:26, ], max_interaction = 2)
glex_rpf <- glex(rp, mtcars[27:32, ])

plot_shap_decomposition(glex_rpf, id = 3, predictors = "hp", threshold = 0.01)
